i.norm: {@link SeekableInMemoryByteChannel#truncate(long)} only shrinks the channel: growing it to a larger size leaves the existing data readable, while a negative target size is rejected with an {@link IllegalArgumentException}.
Truncating to a size larger than the current one keeps the channel readable: the default buffer still has at least one byte available to read.
Truncating beyond Integer.MAX_VALUE is also accepted; the read returns 0 because the single-byte buffer is now full from the previous read.
Any negative target size is invalid and must be rejected.
